clue.text: Cut up after drawing decisive cup tie

parts.note: traitors were hanged, drawn and quartered, so the cutting-up that follows drawing is quartering
a decisive match or round is the final one

explanation.surface: A knockout tie is about to settle who goes through to the next stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The old sentence 'hanged, drawn and quartered' supplies the first part: after drawing came quartering, the cutting into four pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarterfinal is a knockout round in a cup competition, one of the ties leading to the semis.

clue.text: Tart reserving ultimately brisk one for husband?

definitions.text: Tart reserving ultimately brisk one for husband?

indicators.note: one (the Roman numeral I) takes the place of husband (H, its usual abbreviation)
reserving means holding something back inside, so the tart keeps a letter within it

parts.note: a quiche is a savoury open tart

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word brisk

explanation.surface: A suggestive remark about a brief encounter, with a tart involved and a husband swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: K, the last letter of 'brisk', goes inside QUICHE to give QUICKHE; then the H for husband is replaced by I for one. The whole clue doubles as a cheeky description of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickie is a brief sexual encounter, the sort of thing a tart might offer briskly in place of a husband.

clue.text: A team mate so pivotal

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a cricket or football team
an ally is a friend or partner

explanation.surface: A teammate is described as central to the side's success.
explanation.definitionFit: Axially means along or about an axis, the pivot something turns on; 'so pivotal' describes that manner.

clue.text: Hose cap's elevated hole

parts.note: hose is an old word for leg coverings, as in tights

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word cap is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: the top of something is its cap

explanation.surface: A ladder in stockings has been pushed up into a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns TOP (for cap) upwards into POT in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a hole means being in difficulties, an idiom for an awkward situation.

clue.text: Game local to rise and shine

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: in a down light, to rise means the word local is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a British pub is often called the local

explanation.surface: After a game, someone heads to the pub before rising bright and early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns PUB (a British 'local') upwards into BUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub up is to polish something until it shines.

clue.text: Genuine works she's not spotted

indicators.note: works as a verb means operates on or kneads, so the letters of genuine are reshaped

explanation.surface: A genuine person works unseen by anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' signals the anagram of GENUINE. 'not spotted' means unblemished, not unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent young woman, unspotted in the sense of being without blemish or experience.

clue.text: Strip show, tapas and bars in reverse order for the natives

indicators.note: to strip a word here is to remove its outer letters, leaving the middle of show, tapas and bars

explanation.surface: A bar crawl of strip shows and tapas joints is described backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping gives HO, APA and AR; 'in reverse order' says to take them last first: AR + APA + HO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: With royalty included, feather bed a writer

indicators.note: included means placed inside, so the royal letters go within the feather and bed

parts.note: a quill is a large feather
a couch is a bed or sofa
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A writer is pictured with a feather bed fit for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch was an English writer and critic who compiled the Oxford Book of English Verse.

clue.text: Making one's higher education sound as a bell

parts.note: uni is short for university, a place of higher education
a ting is the light ringing sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: Someone's university education is declared perfectly sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy, but here it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniting things means joining them so that they become one.

clue.text: Our origins in theory not humble, exactly

parts.note: big as in self-important, the opposite of humble
bang means exactly, as in bang on time

explanation.surface: A theory of our origins is described as grand and precise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is the theory that the universe began from a single explosive expansion.

clue.text: Like sort of instant bomb-making device

definitions.text: Like sort of instant bomb-making device

parts.words: Like sort of instant bomb-making device
parts.note: making a bomb is slang for making a fortune, so a scheme promising an instant fortune is described as a device for bomb-making

explanation.surface: A gadget for building explosives in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bomb' looks like an explosive, but making a bomb is British slang for earning a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-rich-quick describes a scheme that promises a fortune almost instantly.

clue.text: Pigment permitted a little water

parts.note: lake is a red pigment made from dye
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A painter is allowed a dab of water with the colour.
explanation.walkthrough: LAKE is an artist's pigment, a crimson colour, not a body of water here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lakelet is a small lake, a little body of water.

clue.text: Standard nom de plume the writer leaves for religious books

indicators.note: leaves for says one part departs in favour of another, a swap

parts.note: a nom de plume is a pen name
the writer refers to the setter, me
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An author drops a pen name to write religious books instead.
explanation.walkthrough: In PEN NAME, ME (the setter) leaves and NT takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennant is a flag, and a standard is likewise a flag or banner.

clue.text: Abrasive old comedian

definitions.meaning: a powder or board used for smoothing and polishing
Dick ... was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: A rough-edged comic from years gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a grinding powder, and Dick Emery a well-known British comedian of the past.

clue.text: Sergeant returning in old banger

parts.note: Sgt Pepper is the Beatles' famous sergeant

indicators.note: returning means the words in and old are read backwards

explanation.surface: A police sergeant comes back in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses IN + O to give ONI. 'Banger' is British slang for a sausage, though it suggests an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: Lesser light all one top MP could muster

indicators.note: to muster is to gather and arrange, so these letters are marshalled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A minor figure gathers everyone a leading politician could rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could muster' rearranges ALL + I + TOP into PILOTLA; MP stays as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot lamp is a small indicator light, lesser than a main light.

clue.text: Masculine hand stops fuel being put in bin

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the man's hand fills a gap inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A man's hand stops fuel from going into the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bin' is slang for a psychiatric hospital (loony bin), not a rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: Committal is the act of consigning someone to an institution, such as being put in the bin.

clue.text: After month, roughly cut bird's feathers

indicators.note: after means this comes later, behind the month

parts.note: Mar is short for March

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, losing the last letter

parts.note: about means roughly or approximately

explanation.surface: A month on, someone gives a bird's plumage a rough trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Marabou is the down of the marabou stork, used as trimming.

clue.text: Statement hostelry broadcast or air

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so we use how the hostelry word is pronounced

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
to voice is to air an opinion

explanation.surface: A pub's statement is broadcast or aired.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a statement of charges sent for payment.

clue.text: Water running into view

definitions.meaning: a Scottish river, which flows into its famous firth

explanation.surface: Flowing water comes into sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forth is a Scottish river, and forth means onward or out into view.

clue.text: Penalises opponents for risky card play

parts.note: fines means penalises
South and East are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A card player is penalised for a reckless move.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are N, S, E and W, so any two of them across the table can be opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A finesse is a bridge play in which a lower card is risked in hope of winning the trick.

clue.text: No harm playing around with second language

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged letters surround the next piece
playing means fooling about, so the letters of no harm are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A second language is learned playfully, with no harm done.
explanation.definitionFit: Romansh is a Romance language spoken in parts of Switzerland.

clue.text: Tony clipped hedge before end of summer, bucking current trend

parts.note: tony means posh, and U is the abbreviation for upper-class

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed, so the hedge word loses its last letter

parts.note: privet is a common hedge shrub

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: Someone named Tony trims a hedge at summer's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tony' looks like a name, but it is the adjective meaning stylish, giving U for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upriver means travelling against the flow of the current.

clue.text: Files from drawers — and one other thing

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists who draw
PS, a postscript, adds one more thing to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone takes files out of the drawers, with one more item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' suggests furniture or underwear, but it means artists, RAs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps are coarse files used for shaping wood or metal.

clue.text: Bird caught in a mousetrap losing wings

indicators.note: losing wings means dropping the outer letters, leaving a run inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A bird gets caught in a mousetrap and loses its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinamou is a ground-dwelling bird of Central and South America.

clue.text: This bob designed for short race

indicators.note: designed means put together or arranged, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A new bob haircut is designed for a short dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbits are a race of small people in Tolkien's fiction.

clue.text: As nice as pie? About right

definitions.text: As nice as pie? About right

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece
pie is printers' slang for jumbled type, so the words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A poisoner's sweet remark that something is as nice as pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers' 'pie' is jumbled type, so AS NICE is scrambled around R. The whole clue hints at arsenic put into a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a poison, ironically as nice as pie when baked into one.

clue.text: Subjects annually addressed in this college lecture

parts.note: Queens' is a Cambridge college and Queen's an Oxford one
a lecture is a speech

explanation.surface: A college lecture is given every year to its students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subjects' looks like academic topics, but it means the monarch's subjects, addressed at the State Opening of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen's Speech is the annual address in which the monarch tells subjects the government's plans.
